parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Define the Young modulus of a material.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem: A metal wire P that obeys Hooke's law is stretched within its limit of proportionality.
parts.text:
On Fig. 4.1, sketch the variation of tensile force $F$ in the wire with its extension $x$.
{{figure:figure_4_1.png}}

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: State the name of the quantity represented by the gradient of the line in Fig. 4.1.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: State the name of the quantity represented by the area under the line in Fig. 4.1.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Another wire Q is made from a metal that has twice the Young modulus of the metal of wire P in (b). Wire Q has the same volume as wire P but has double the cross-sectional area of wire P.

The two wires are extended by equal tensile forces within their limits of proportionality.

State and explain how the extension of wire Q compares with the extension of wire P.
